verification.scope: complete guarded_bytes integration test binary; three new tests
complete root_result_reader integration test binary; two new tests and all existing unary probes

behavior: A fixed eight-descriptor same-thread oracle records actual System allocation pointer, complete Layout and ordinal; it records free only after System.dealloc returns.
Actual one-byte Bytes aliases map by address range to their unique live backing, rather than choosing the last allocation with the same size.

The original worker process credit is still Blocked after all nonfinal aliases exit; original guard observes post-dealloc before its original credit field releases, after which complete capacity can be granted again.
Actual tonic unary Data uses its complete SEGMENT encoder backing despite a short wire body; all nonfinal clones/slices retain backing and original root/process-credit holders.
The actual ACK decoder and send buffers both have descriptors; decoder free and live DATA ordinal are separate even under valid address reuse.
ACK retires Data before projection and retains fixed metadata owners; its test does not falsely require the already returned process Data position to stay blocked.
Actual ninth allocation overflows the fixed oracle and keeps successful-reclamation evidence permanently invalid even after all allocations are dropped.
component_boundary: Actual System Layout/capacity and same-thread post-return frees are proved for these selected owned allocations, not malloc usable size, RSS, allocator cache or all engine allocations.
The worker test directly observes original credit callback ordering; unary callback ordering also relies on the unchanged production GuardedOwner field order.
Selected component tonic bodies are not live H2/listener/FE or 1FE+3BE; there is no cross-thread last-drop claim.
Fixed Bytes wrapper metadata remains the existing ADR-0168 exception and frees after guard exit; no vendor patch or second wallet is introduced.
remaining_open: Closing old/new copy coexistence, actual peak and returnable failure rollback.
